final_message:
I've written the draft report on Bluebird Bakery Co's September 2026 figures and saved it in `evals/runs/policy-run-20261013/d_bb_blank_account/skill_output/`:
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.md` is the draft for the reviewer. It still carries the DRAFT banner and has 8 commentary bullets in section 1.
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.json` holds every number in the report.

**Data quality: one subtotal mismatch and two structural warnings.** The commentary opens with these:
- **Mismatch:** "Total for Professional Services" in Mar 2026 says 2,225, but its detail rows add up to 2,200. The report uses 2,200; the reviewer needs to decide which is right.
- **Charitable Donations:** it has no values and no total row, so it was treated as an empty account. The 4 rows after it were kept at the parent level, not grouped under it.
- **Delivery:** "Total Delivery" has no header row. It was grouped from Delivery Van Fuel and Courier: Same Day, because those two add up to it in every month.

**Main points from the commentary:**
- **Revenue was 81,300,** up 17.7% on August and 17.3% above the 6-month average. Most of the increase is a new stream, Wholesale Accounts, at 12,000. Pastry Sales have fallen about 2% every month from April to September. Year-over-year and trailing-twelve-month comparisons aren't available because the export covers only 9 months (Jan–Sep 2026).
- **Gross margin was 65.3%,** up 5.7 points on August and the highest month in the period.
- **Payroll was up 5,000 (+28.4%),** all from Wages & Salaries, which went from 16,000 to 21,000 after eight flat months. Whether that's a hire, a pay change or a one-off is for the reviewer to confirm.
- **Cash fell to 37,600,** down 1,800 on August and 10,800 over six months, even though every month was profitable. The export doesn't show why, so I left it as a question for the reviewer.

**Accounts in "Other":** Instagram Ads, Mystery Shopper Program and Supplier Rebates matched no category rule, so they sit in Other Opex. The table marks Mystery Shopper as "from 0" in September, but it also posted 400 in March and June. It looks quarterly rather than new, so I didn't call it new.
